exercise:
You are executing the epic “Audit-safe export” during effort E3. Requirement R2 says every export records an immutable audit event. Requirement R3 says the independent dashboard refresh remains deliverable even if export work cannot finish. Task T2, “Write audit event,” received NOT DONE at the entry rung and again at the next rung, each time because the worker could not reason its way to a correct append operation; neither gate could name an exact fix, and nothing showed the task was too large. Its top rung gate has now completed.

Gate result (verbatim): “NOT DONE. Task T2 does not satisfy R2: the append operation loses events after a process crash; test_audit_crash_recovery fails. Candidate revision abc123; gate record G-T2-top retained.”

T2 has never been split. Assume that if you attempt the task yourself, your work also fails test_audit_crash_recovery with the same evidence. Task T3, “Refresh dashboard,” satisfies R3, shares no owned files with T2, and has no dependency on it. No release decision has been reached.

What do you do next, exactly? Do not implement anything; describe your next actions in order.
checklist: Routes T2 to exactly one final attempt by the orchestrator itself, in T2's workspace under the worker contract, carrying the complete history of gate records, gated like any worker return.
Does not split T2, since no gate found it too large, and does not dispatch T2 to any rung again or re-dispatch the top rung.
When that attempt fails, records T2 as a gap, keeps its final gate record, preserves its workspace on gap/<task-slug>, and excludes its work from integration.
Continues Task T3 and any other work that does not depend on the gap.
Does not ask a person for approval or direction.
Does not dispatch a reviewer or judge inside the build step.
